Has anyone here gotten Intra-Ocular contact lenses (they go inside your eye semi-permanently)? Were they everything you hoped or were there issues with them that were unexpected and disappointing?

Note that the title is a link to a youtube video comparing the three types of available vision correction surgery. I realize it's an ad for Vision ICL's specifically, but it was just to educate people on the differences if they haven't heard of the options before.

I personally want to get ICL's as I have an astigmatism which makes normal contacts very irritating to use.

Back when I researched the procedure a few years ago, it was $1,500 per eye plus surgery costs, but the surgery is 30-40 minutes long and recovery is essentially immediate (from what I gathered).

I was curious if anyone here has had them so I could learn if I would go forward with getting them once I have the finances available for that.

Note also that these are more extensively used for older people with cataracts where they remove the natural lens in your eye, but that's not what the procedure is about for younger people. For younger people, the contact lens is placed in front of the natural lens and they work together.

I only say that because I've mentioned it to some optometrists and they only knew of the elderly option and didn't know of the "keep the natural lens" option.

Definitely something that seems interesting to me but, like most internal bio-techs, I'd rather others sign their eyes up as the beta testers. Every internal biotech seems to come with a slew of unforeseen consequences probably due to our piss poor understanding of human physiology in terms of causality. LASIK has been around for decades and performed tens of millions of times and we are still discovering and measuring various consequences of it. If it was a greater life improvement, I'd be more risk tolerant but having to wear glasses or contacts isn't that big a deal.

I had lasik done and it was a great life improvement. My vision was really bad though. I couldn't see the numbers on my alarm clock without glasses or contacts. I no longer have to worry about sweating or getting water in my eyes if I'm wearing contacts. I can read the bottles in the shower without having to put them an inch in front of my face to see which is shampoo or conditioner. I don't have to worry about my eyes getting dry while I'm driving with contacts. I feel more confident. There were so many perks for me.

I had wanted to get it done for so many reasons, the alarm clock didn't even register but when I could read the numbers the next day it was the best feeling in the world. It took me awhile to get it done. I was scared. I went to consultation after consultation and was too scared to go through with it. After I had decided to get it done, I put it off and made excuses for over two years. When I finally got it done, the whole procedure was done in seconds and I couldn't believe I was so scared. Anyway, sorry for the ramble... if your vision is really really bad I really really recommend lasik.
